en.headline: Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank to open office in Hong Kong
en.dek: The government and the bank signed agreements on Saturday; Hong Kong will contribute a further US$20 million to the bank's project preparation fund.
body: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank will establish an office in Hong Kong after the central government and the bank signed an agreement on Saturday laying the foundation for the move.

Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the decision was a clear recognition of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre and its role in pooling international capital for Asian infrastructure. He pledged full government support for the office's establishment and operation.

Under a second agreement signed the same day, Hong Kong will contribute a further US$20 million to the bank's Project Preparation Special Fund, bringing its total contribution to US$30 million after an initial US$10 million in 2018. Acting Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Joseph Chan signed that pact with an AIIB official.

Hong Kong has been a member of the 111-member multilateral development bank since 2017. The government said it would introduce subsidiary legislation to the Legislative Council to confer the necessary privileges and immunities on the new office.

zh.headline: 亞投行將在港設辦公室 陳茂波指彰顯國際金融中心地位
zh.dek: 中央政府與亞投行周六簽署協定奠定設辦基礎，香港再向項目準備特別基金注資2000萬美元。
body: 亞洲基礎設施投資銀行將在香港設立辦公室。中央政府與亞投行周六簽署協定，為在港設辦奠定基礎，協定由財政部部長藍佛安與亞投行行長鄒加怡代表簽署。
財政司司長陳茂波表示，亞投行選擇在港設辦，充分肯定香港作為國際金融中心的地位，並彰顯香港在匯聚國際資本、支持亞洲基建方面的獨特角色。特區政府會全力支持辦公室的設立和運作。
同日，署理財經事務及庫務局局長陳浩濂代表特區政府與亞投行簽署另一份協定，向項目準備特別基金再注資2000萬美元，連同2018年的1000萬美元，總貢獻達3000萬美元。
香港自2017年起成為亞投行成員。政府表示，將盡早向立法會提交有關附屬法例，以正式賦予辦公室所需的特權及豁免。
